To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nomograms are the best available decision aid in the field of urology.

(i) nomograms are superior to all other decision aids for the prediction of outcome in urological malignancy; (ii) nomograms provide individual‐level estimates that facilitate evidence‐based, patient‐specific decision‐making; and (iii) nomograms are easy to use and can be implemented into electronic patient‐record systems.
nomograms are superior decision aids to other tools.

the development and validation of nomograms for predicting the outcome of various urological malignances.
the development of nomograms for predicting the outcome in patients with prostate cancer, renal cell carcinoma and testicular cancer.
the development of nomograms for predicting treatment outcomes in prostate cancer, renal cell cancer, bladder cancer, testicular cancer, and penile cancer.

nomograms are superior to other prediction models, but this is not the case for all prediction models.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nomograms can provide accurate estimates of the likelihood for a particular outcome, which is superior to the estimates provided by risk grouping systems, CART analysis, probability tables and ANNs.
nomograms are superior to other prediction methods in terms of their ability to provide highly accurate and individualized risk estimates for the purpose of decision-making.

nomograms provide individualised evidence-based and highly accurate risk predictions.
